subject: Hosted Rate Card vs Dedicated/Private — delta matrix & discount levers
messages:
From: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acmedata.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Rate card + baseline questions for hosted -> Dedicated/Private

Hi Karthik / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers look promising. Procurement has two asks before we can move forward with a POC: a simple delta matrix that shows how your hosted API baseline rates translate to Dedicated (reserved pool) and Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments, and the discount levers (commit, term, volume tiers, support package) you typically offer.

I've attached our expected usage profile (monthly tokens by workload) and a short procurement checklist. High level questions:
- For high-traffic realtime chat (avg seq len 400 tokens), what is the per-token baseline on hosted, and how does that map to an effective per-token for Dedicated at 50% and 80% utilization?
- For Private, do you provide a license + infra amortization example so we can model TCO?
- What minimum commit or term is required for deeper discounts?

Can you send a concise matrix (one page) we can include in our procurement package? Appreciate a response by close of week if possible.

Attachments: acme-rate-request-20260512.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Jared

Jared — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file. Forwarding to Neha (pricing/solutions) and Marcus (dedicated capacity) to draft a delta matrix.

Quick replies to your bullets:
- Hosted baseline: we'll give you a host-to-hosted breakdown (prompt vs completion buckets) and an example blended per-token.
- Dedicated: we show modeled effective per-token at different utilization rates — there are three levers that change the math: reserved GPU commit, autoscale burst costs, and prefix/KV cache hit rates.
- Private: we'll include a simple 3-year amortized TCO (license + infra + ops) and example quantization/instance mixes.

We'll aim to deliver a one-page delta matrix + short notes by Thursday EOD PT. If you have a preferred format for the procurement doc, send it and we'll align.

Karthik

Subject: FW: Rate card + baseline questions for hosted -> Dedicated/Private

Hi Jared — attaching a working delta matrix and notes. See the quick summary below; full spreadsheet in the attachment.

Summary (high level):
- Hosted (public API): list rates = $0.0008 / prompt token, $0.0016 / completion token (example model family). Blended example (chat) = ~$0.0011 / token.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): effective per-token depends on commit and utilization. Example: with a 6-month reserved commit for 4x A100 GPUs at 75% utilization and expected batching/KV cache hit = 15% token reduction, modeled blended cost = ~$0.00055 / token (after infrastructure and reserved overhead).
- Private (customer-managed infra): baseline is license + infra. Example 3-year amortization for equivalent throughput: license + support = $X/year (see spreadsheet), infra amortized = $Y/year => effective blended token cost ~ $0.00045-$0.00065 depending on infra choice and ops headcount.

Discount levers:
- Volume/commit: 10% at $250k/yr, 18% at $500k/yr, 25%+ with multi-year enterprise commit and platform + support bundles.
- Term: 12 vs 36 month term gives step changes to both list rates and license amortization assumptions.
- Add-ons: premium SLOs, private control plane, and enhanced retention are priced as addons and often negotiated into the commit.

Notes about assumptions: model assumes average sequence length 400 tokens, 60% ratio prompt:completion, 15% KV/prefix cache hits, and continuous batching that reduces per-token kernel overhead. We'll surface sensitivity rows in the attached spreadsheet.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-v3.pdf (pdf), dedicated-config-sample.yaml (yaml)

Neha

Subject: Re: Rate card + baseline questions for hosted -> Dedicated/Private

Thanks — very helpful. Couple of follow-ups before we circulate internally:
1) For the Dedicated example: can you show both 50% and 90% utilization scenarios? Our CFO wants to understand downside (low utilization) risk.
2) For Private: can you give a worked example that includes ops FTE (1.0 FTE) vs 0.25 FTE (managed ops) so we can see OPEX delta?
3) Discount ask: Acme is prepared to commit $400k ARR over 24 months if we can get to ~20% discount vs hosted list and a predictable cap on autoscale burst costs. Is that in scope?

Also — do you require a signed NDA before sharing the full license headcount/non-public price? We can get legal to expedite if needed.

Best,
Jared
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + baseline questions for hosted -> Dedicated/Private

Jared — great context and thanks for the target commit number. We've produced an updated one-page delta matrix and two worked scenarios (50% / 90% util) plus the Private TCO with ops FTE sensitivity. Attached are: 1) one-page delta matrix PDF, 2) Dedicated utilization workbook, and 3) Private TCO (ops sensitivity).

Quick answers:
- Dedicated: at 50% util modeled blended token = $0.00078 (reserve + burst amortized); at 90% util = $0.00042. We included a pessimistic 35% batch/cache improvement vs optimistic 20% so you can see the range.
- Private: with 1.0 FTE ops included the blended token sits near $0.00070; with 0.25 FTE (managed ops) it drops to ~$0.00050 — biggest drivers are infra refresh cadence and quantization options.
- Discount ask: $400k ARR over 24 months -> we can offer 18% off hosted list with a committed reserved-capacity SKU and a capped autoscale burn rate (we'll cap bursts at a fixed multiplier for billing). To reach 20%+ we'd need either a 36-month term or an expanded platform bundle (observability retention + enterprise SSO).

NDA: we don't require a separate NDA to share the redlined license numbers in the updated attachments; the pricing workbook contains non-public license lines — if you prefer we can route that via an NDA'ed DocuSign.

Next steps:
- I'll follow up with a short commercial summary for Legal/Finance (1 page) and the pricing workbook exported as XLSX. Can we aim to have Legal back to you by next Wednesday?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
